acceptance: Record a decision: keep one plan per (query, stream, test_type), or retain per-iteration plans when fingerprints differ.
If retaining, store only differing plans, keep existing consumers (loader, show-plan, compare, MCP, Explorer viewer) working, and add a test with two iterations whose plans differ.
Either way, docs state what a bundle can and cannot tell about cross-iteration plan stability.
context: Arose from PR #3711 review. SQL capture already captures each distinct executed SQL once, so the gap matters mainly for engines whose plan can change between identical executions.
description: The plans companion now stores one entry per (query, stream, test_type) and records the iteration and run_type it came from; reloaded results attach the plan only to that row. Per-iteration keys were tried and reverted because they broke the one-entry contract. Consequence: plans of other iterations of the same query and stream are not stored, so plan stability across iterations (for example adaptive engines or warmup vs measurement) cannot be checked from a bundle.
